facts.text: Holyrood Abbey, founded by David I in 1128, sits at the foot of the Royal Mile and was originally called the Church of the Holy Rude.
The Palace of Holyroodhouse, now the monarch’s Scottish residence, grew from the abbey’s cloister precinct into a Renaissance palace.
Holyrood Park, a sprawling royal park to the south and east of the palace, offers one of Scotland’s largest interactive science centres, Dynamic Earth.
Walking through the abbey nave and gardens after touring the palace lets visitors see the only surviving east processional doorway from David I’s original monastery.
Holyrood’s name comes from the Scots term for ‘Holy Cross’, reflecting the abbey’s original dedication to the Holy Rude.
The area’s modern identity includes the Scottish Parliament Building, making Holyrood a metonym for the Scottish Government in contemporary media.
